instructions.question: Did this CI run fail because of a transient problem rather than a defect in the change?
instructions.focus: Read the tails of the failing job logs in `ci_logs` (each job is introduced by a line starting with `### `). Decide whether re-running the same jobs would plausibly pass without any code change.
flaky_signals: Network or registry timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, rate limits (HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504) while downloading packages, images or actions
The runner was lost, cancelled, out of disk or out of memory, or the job hit its time limit while the steps before it were healthy
An intermittent test failure that names no assertion about the changed dependency, such as a timing race or a port already in use
A package or image that could not be fetched from the upstream service
real_signals: A compile, type, lint or formatting error
A test assertion that fails with a concrete expected and actual value
A dependency resolution conflict, a missing or removed package version or a failing checksum
An error that names the updated dependency or its API
The same failure is plausible on every run

criteria.flaky: The logs show a transient infrastructure or network problem, and re-running the failed jobs would plausibly pass.
criteria.real: The logs show a deterministic failure in the code, the tests, the build or the dependency itself.
criteria.unsure: The logs are empty, cut off before the failure, or do not make the cause clear.
